text:
anya: Quick check — I ran a new cross-encoder reranker on prod-queries-v2 this morning and NDCG@10 dropped ~3.2% vs our current bi-encoder+re-rank baseline. MRR also dipped. Posting the raw metrics I got below, any obvious suspects?

sam: Can you paste the eval command and the metric table?

anya: Sure — eval harness run: `python eval/rerank_eval.py --model xce-bert-base-v2 --data data/prod-queries-v2.jsonl --truncate 512 --batch 64`

anya: Metrics:```
baseline (bi-encoder+rerank): NDCG@10=0.722, MRR=0.614
cross-encoder (xce-bert-base-v2): NDCG@10=0.699, MRR=0.588
quantized int8: NDCG@10=0.693, MRR=0.582
```

eval-bot: FYI I flagged that prod-queries-v2 has 18% queries with only 1 labeled positive. Label sparsity can make NDCG unstable. :warning:

sam: A few quick things to check: 1) Query/document canonicalization (site prefixes, punctuation), 2) candidate pool differences (did you use same negative sampling?), 3) tokenization/truncation differences. Cross-encoders are sensitive to exact formatting.

leo: Also check whether you accidentally deduped docs for the baseline but not for the CE run — that kills recall.

anya: I used the candidate pool we index in prod (top-100 from bi-encoder). For the CE run I accidentally re-generated candidates with a slightly different tokenizer setting — could that explain ~3%?

mike: Yes, if the candidate pool changed you'll see big swings. CE should improve re-ordering, not reduce recall if pool is identical. Re-run with identical candidates.

sam: Another common trap: our eval pipeline strips HTML in the baseline path but not in the CE path if you ran the new preproc. Compare `preproc.normalize_text()` usage.

anya: Good catch. I think I toggled a normalization flag when experimenting with truncation. Will re-run. For the quantized run — int8 — the drop is small but consistent. Anyone seen int8 causing ranking regressions?

leo: We've seen tiny score calibration shifts with int8 that affect thresholds. Usually post-calibration (rescaling logits) recovers most of it. Also watch pooling (CLS vs mean) — different implementations between FP32 and quantized kernels can matter.

mike: Action items: (1) anya will re-run CE with identical candidates and normalized text, (2) run CE FP32 vs int8 on the exact same inputs to isolate quantization error, (3) add NDCG@1, @5, @10 and per-query delta histogram so we know if a few queries blow up. I'll add a small eval job to the queue and tag results to #eng-ml.

anya: Thanks — re-running now. I will also dump a sample of queries with worst delta for inspection and post here.

sam: When you post samples, include both original query, normalized query, doc title, and doc snippet. Helps spot formatting mismatches.

anya: Will do. Posting preliminary sample in a follow-up thread. :mag:

eval-bot: job rerank-repro-1729543210 started by anya — status: queued

mike: If the re-run still shows regression, let's run a small AB where we keep bi-encoder candidate pool but swap the reranker only, and measure user-level metric (CTR or downstream accept). Otherwise could be dataset artifact.

anya: Got it. Thanks everyone.
